actual_scope: For a helper boundary with proper terminal 0<T<D and contact-free paths 0<=a_i<=b_i<=D, prove that one path with b>T gives a strictly decreasing rank bill on [a,T], that the terminal value is nonpositive for every path set, that all paths starting at zero with at least one crossing path give a negative interior bill, and exhibit four crossing paths where an interior dimension beats both endpoints.
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether a legal causal split improves the complete P104 productive/paid invoice. The predecessor #7283 proves the endpoint maximum only for a boundary from dimension 0 to D and leaves the proper terminal open. This package answers that boundary case of the rank-bill factor. It does not emit a cut, price an ordinary bill, or change the selected exponent, so the invoice question stays open.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the rank-bill factor of a helper split. A proper terminal is the remaining geometric case in which a new intermediate chart could change that factor. A positive G is still short of a legal paid-profile improvement.
stop_rule: Stop after the one-path theorem, the terminal and zero-start propositions, the four-path counterexample and the stated finite censuses. Do not search the 68-split word, emit a chart, or rerun frontier7000.
evidence: PROOF.md is the general argument for 0<t<1 and every proper terminal. verify.py certifies the four-path counterexample with integer square-root arithmetic, replays the three propositions and Theorem 1 on the stated finite grids, and rejects four forged claims. Marker PASS_PROPER_TERMINAL_HELPER_RANK_BILL.

open_questions.question: Can a positive proper-terminal rank bill appear at an interior dimension when both endpoint values are nonpositive?
open_questions.why_it_matters: If not, the two-endpoint comparison still decides whether a proper terminal can give a rank-bill gain even though it does not give the maximum.
open_questions.first_step: Fix four crossing paths and determine the sign structure of the unique interior critical point, or prove a maximum principle for the tent decomposition in PROOF.md.
open_questions.blocked_by: The four-path witness has a negative interior maximum. A floating-point search over four million configurations found no positive interior value with nonpositive endpoints, but that is not a proof.

open_questions.question: Is the endpoint maximum true for exactly two and exactly three crossing paths?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Theorem 1 proves one path and the four-path counterexample excludes the general statement. Two and three paths decide where the threshold lies.
open_questions.first_step: Extend the verifier census or find an explicit two-path or three-path witness for larger D and a finer rational grid.
open_questions.blocked_by: The stated exhaustive grids (D<=8 for two paths, D<=7 for three) find no interior win, and they are finite censuses, not proofs.
